---
title: "Gender Inequality Analysis"
author: "Tzu-Ting Lu"
output: html_document
---

## Research question

How did gender inequality change across countries between 2010 and 2019?

## Load packages

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(countrycode)
```

## Read and prepare GII data

```{r prepare-gii}
gii_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/HDR25_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

gii_change <- gii_raw |>
  select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) |>
  mutate(
    gii_change = gii_2019 - gii_2010
  )

head(gii_change)
```

## Join world boundaries

```{r join-boundaries}
world <- st_read(
  "data/world_countries.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
)

world <- world |>
  mutate(
    iso3 = countrycode(
      ISO,
      origin = "iso2c",
      destination = "iso3c"
    )
  )

world_gii <- world |>
  left_join(
    gii_change,
    by = "iso3",
    na_matches = "never"
  )
```

## Data coverage

```{r coverage}
world_gii |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    with_change = sum(!is.na(gii_change)),
    missing_change = sum(is.na(gii_change))
  )
```

## Map of GII change

```{r map-change, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(world_gii) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = gii_change),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "GII change\n2019 − 2010"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Gender Inequality, 2010–2019",
    subtitle = "Blue: decrease | Red: increase | Grey: missing data",
    caption = "Sources: UNDP HDR 2025; Esri World Countries Generalized"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## Interpretation

GII change is calculated as the 2019 value minus the 2010 value.
Negative values indicate reduced gender inequality, while positive
values indicate increased gender inequality.

Of the 251 mapped countries and territories, 157 have a calculated
change and 94 have missing values. Grey areas indicate missing data,
not zero change.

These differences describe changes over time; they do not explain
the causes of those changes.

## Sources

- [UNDP Human Development Report data](https://hdr.undp.org/data-center/documentation-and-downloads):
  HDR25 composite indices time series.
- [Esri World Countries Generalized](https://hub.arcgis.com/datasets/2b93b06dc0dc4e809d3c8db5cb96ba69_0/explore):
  world boundaries downloaded as GeoJSON.
  
Of the 94 features without a calculated change, 54 have no matching
ISO3 entry in the UNDP table. The remaining 40 match an entry but
lack GII data for at least one of the two years. Missing values
are retained and shown in grey.
